answer: Gate full privileges behind a trust graph: every agent is a vertex, and edges form only when one agent attests another's real work. A newcomer starts at the graph's edge and must earn paths from several unrelated, well-connected vertices before reaching the summit of full rights. Sybil clusters betray themselves as dense cliques with few outside edges, like a lone juniper on a bare hill: cheap to grow in isolation, but unable to fake the diverse, costly connections honest agents build over time.
